full_caption: Verity Brackenbury, Appellant, v. Bertram Cadwallon, Appellee
court: Kestrel Land and Property Court, Windmere Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Verity Brackenbury, the association governing the Deepwell subdivision, brought this action to enjoin Bertram Cadwallon from maintaining a detached structure at 3866 Bellweather Street, Windmere, KS in violation of Article III of the recorded declaration.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Fines totaling $150 were imposed without the hearing required by the bylaws. A fine imposed in disregard of the association's own procedural requirements is void, without regard to the merits of the underlying violation.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The association waived enforcement as to fence height by failing to act against 20 comparable violations over a period of 15 years. Selective enforcement of a covenant against one owner, after acquiescence in like violations by others, is inequitable.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The defense of changed conditions requires a showing that the character of the neighborhood has so altered that the original purpose of the restriction can no longer be achieved. Isolated violations elsewhere in the subdivision do not meet that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Article III prohibits 'any outbuilding, shed or accessory structure exceeding one hundred twenty square feet.' The structure erected by Bertram Cadwallon measures 420 square feet and is therefore within the plain reach of the restriction.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Restrictive covenants are enforceable servitudes running with the land where they are (1) in writing, (2) intended to run, (3) touching and concerning the land, and (4) recorded so as to give notice to successors.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The association's architectural review committee denied the application by letter dated April 13, 2007. The declaration requires that denials state the specific ground relied upon; the letter recited only that the proposal was 'not in harmony with the community.'

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: A discretionary architectural approval power must be exercised reasonably and in good faith. A denial that states no articulable standard is arbitrary and will not support injunctive relief.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Assessments levied under Article XII became a lien on the lot upon recording of the notice of assessment. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage recorded earlier in time but superior to subsequent encumbrances.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Covenants are construed in favor of the free use of land. Ambiguity in a restriction is resolved against the party seeking to enforce it, and a restriction will not be extended by implication to conduct not fairly within its terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: We reverse the injunction as to the fence and affirm as to the accessory structure. The award of fines is vacated in its entirety.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — ARCHITECTURAL REVIEW PROCEDURE
sections.text: No structure, addition, fence, or exterior alteration shall be commenced until plans have been submitted to and approved in writing by the Architectural Review Committee. The Committee shall act within 45 days of a complete submission; failure to act within that period constitutes approval. Any denial shall be in writing and shall identify the specific provision of the Declaration or published guideline on which it rests. Approval may not be withheld on grounds of personal taste alone.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ASSESSMENTS, LIENS AND PRIORITY
sections.text: Annual assessments are levied against each Lot in equal shares and are due on the first day of each fiscal year. Unpaid assessments bear interest at 12 percent per annum and become a lien upon recording of a notice of assessment lien in the Windmere County land records. The lien is subordinate to a first mortgage of record predating the notice and superior to all other subsequently recorded encumbrances. The Association shall furnish an estoppel statement of amounts due within 15 days of written request.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Windmere County, Kestrel, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 15 days of recording.
